## The partition solver for disjoint vapour-cloud pairs (`uv-solver: partition`) {#sec-ch04-uv-partition}

### Summary

When every reaction of the card turns one vapour into one condensate and no species takes part in two reactions,
the fixed-energy problem of @sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv has a much simpler structure: at any trial temperature each
pair's split between vapour and cloud is known in closed form (all of the inventory as vapour if that is below
saturation, the saturated amount otherwise), so the only unknown is the temperature, fixed by the energy. This
solver exploits that: it brackets the root of the energy residual in temperature by halving or doubling, then takes
safeguarded Newton steps inside the bracket. It is the default first attempt (`uv-solver: auto`) for such cards, the
Uranus-like methane and hydrogen-sulfide cards among them, and it falls back to the constrained-least-squares
kernel when it cannot bracket or converge.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Solve the fixed-energy problem for disjoint pairs through the scalar equation @eq-ch04-uv-partition-energy
with the closed-form split @eq-ch04-uv-partition-split.

**Data.** Same as @sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv; the gain returned is zero (no active block), `diag` the iteration count
or $-1$ on a forced-partition failure.

**Placement.** Inside `equilibrate_uv`, before its own iteration, when the solver code is `auto` or `partition`.

**Activation.** `uv-solver: partition` (forced; a non-partitionable network is refused at the call) or `auto`
(default; falls back). Eligibility is decided once in `reset` from the stoichiometric matrix.

**Guarantee / limits.** Energy closed to $64\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\max(|U_0|, 1)$; inventories exact; the slope used
in the Newton step is the exact derivative only when the extra caloric functions do not depend on concentration.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: the three solver settings agree on recorded states; inline and named curves
agree bit for bit under this solver; CUDA equals CPU.
:::

Local symbols: for pair $j$ with reaction $a_j V_j \to b_j C_j$, $N_j = c_{V_j} + (a_j/b_j)\,c_{C_j}$ the
reaction-invariant inventory [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$] (`totals`); $c^{\mathrm{sat}}_{V_j}(T)$ the saturated vapour
concentration; $F(T) = U(T) - U_0$ the energy residual [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$]; $F'_{\mathrm{used}}$ the slope the solver
uses; $[T_{\mathrm{lo}}, T_{\mathrm{hi}}]$ the bracket. The internal names are `partition_uv_state` (the split and
its energy at one temperature) and `equilibrate_uv_partition` (the scalar solve).

### Derivation

**The split.** For pair $j$ the saturation condition $a_j\ln(c_{V_j}\mathcal R T) = L_j(T)$ gives the saturated
vapour concentration, and the inventory $N_j$ is what the reaction cannot change:
$$
c^{\mathrm{sat}}_{V_j}(T) = \frac{\exp\bigl(L_j(T)/a_j\bigr)}{\mathcal R T}, \qquad
c_{V_j}(T) = \min\bigl(N_j, c^{\mathrm{sat}}_{V_j}(T)\bigr), \qquad
c_{C_j}(T) = \frac{b_j}{a_j}\bigl(N_j - c_{V_j}(T)\bigr) ,
$$ {#eq-ch04-uv-partition-split}
which is the complementarity condition of @sec-ch04-conditions solved explicitly: either the whole inventory is
vapour and undersaturated, or the vapour is saturated and the rest is cloud. A pair with $N_j = 0$ has both set to
zero. @eq-ch04-uv-partition-split is computed in `partition_uv_state`
({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h partition_uv_state >}}); species that belong to no pair keep their
concentrations. The energy of the split state and its temperature derivative are
$$
\begin{aligned}
F(T) &= \sum_i c_i(T)\,u_i(T) - U_0, \\
F'_{\mathrm{used}}(T) &= \sum_i c_i(T)\,u_i'(T) + \sum_{j:\,c_{V_j} < N_j}
\frac{\mathrm dc_{V_j}}{\mathrm dT}\Bigl(u_{V_j} - \frac{b_j}{a_j}u_{C_j}\Bigr), \qquad
\frac{\mathrm dc_{V_j}}{\mathrm dT} = c_{V_j}\Bigl(\frac{L'_j}{a_j} - \frac1T\Bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-uv-partition-energy}
where the second sum is the latent contribution of every pair that is on its saturation curve (a pair that is all
vapour has a constant $c_{V_j}$ and contributes nothing) and the derivative of the saturated concentration is
`[C1]` of `uv_partition_check.py`. @eq-ch04-uv-partition-energy is computed in the same `partition_uv_state`. The
slope is the exact $\mathrm dF/\mathrm dT$ when the extra caloric functions of @sec-ch03-caloric are
thermodynamically consistent and independent of concentration, which is the case for the baseline (none at the
pin); otherwise it is the slope the implementation uses, as the in-tree note says.

**The scalar solve.** Starting from the driver's temperature, `equilibrate_uv_partition`
({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_uv.h equilibrate_uv_partition >}}) evaluates $F$; if $\lvert F\rvert$ exceeds the tolerance
$64\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\max(|U_0|, 1)$ it brackets a sign change by halving the temperature while $F > 0$ or
doubling it while $F < 0$ (at most 64 steps), then iterates
$$
T \leftarrow T - \frac{F(T)}{F'_{\mathrm{used}}(T)}, \quad \text{replaced by } \tfrac12(T_{\mathrm{lo}} + T_{\mathrm{hi}})
\text{ when the step is not finite or leaves the bracket},
$$ {#eq-ch04-uv-partition-newton}
updating the bracket from the sign of $F$ after each step, until $\lvert F\rvert$ is within tolerance or `max-iter` is
reached (the initial evaluation counts as the first iteration). @eq-ch04-uv-partition-newton is computed in
`equilibrate_uv_partition`. On success the gain is zero, `nactive` is zero and `diag` is the iteration count; on
failure the pre-partition state is restored and the caller decides: `auto` runs the constrained-least-squares
kernel, `partition` returns status 2 with a printed warning and `diag` $= -1$.

The inventories are exact by construction (`[C3]`), and the energy is closed to the stated tolerance
($1.2\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ against $2.4\times10^{-10}$ on the water example). On the same state the
partition solver and the constrained-least-squares branch agree in temperature and cloud amount to $10^{-7}$
relative (`[C2]`: $314.1149\,\mathrm K$ from both), the difference being their different stopping rules. The
eligibility rule (`[C4]`) is evaluated once per module: the Jupiter card is not partitionable (ammonia in two
reactions), the methane and hydrogen-sulfide card is, a reaction with a gaseous product is not. The check is
`uv_partition_check.py`, a numpy port of both functions that reuses the state of `equilibrate_uv_check.py`.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch04-uv-partition-energy shows $F(T)$ for the water example: a straight line where the pair is all vapour
(constant heat capacity, no latent term), a steeper curve where the pair is saturated, and the iterates of the
bracket-and-Newton search. The kink at the temperature where the inventory just fits is where $F'$ jumps; the
safeguard keeps the Newton step inside the bracket across it. Per cell the work is one evaluation of every curve
per iteration and no linear algebra, which is why this branch is tried first. The function is evaluated with the
same per-cell arena as the main kernel and runs under the same dispatch.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch04-uv-partition-energy
#| fig-cap: "The energy residual of the partitioned state against trial temperature for the water example of the fixed-energy check (blue), with the kink where the whole inventory fits in the vapour, and the iterates of the partition solver (green circles; the first three are numbered from the start, and iterates 3 to 6 share one label where they sit on the solution; the dotted grey line is the solution). Above the kink the pair is all vapour and the residual is linear in temperature; below it the pair is saturated and the latent term steepens the curve."
#| fig-alt: "A curve of energy residual in kilojoules per cubic metre against temperature from 260 to 320 K, crossing zero near 314 K, with a visible change of slope near 318 K. Numbered circles mark the first three iterates and one label marks the cluster at the zero crossing."
#| echo: false
from kintera_report.ch04.figures.fig_uv_partition_energy import make_fig
make_fig()
```

Eligibility is computed in `ThermoYImpl::reset` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}): for each
reaction, exactly one gas with a negative coefficient and exactly one condensate with a positive one, every
coefficient finite, and no species used twice; the result is the member `uv_partitionable`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoYImpl::uv_partitionable >}}). The two coefficients $a_j$ and $b_j$ may differ
from one.

: Code map of the partition solver. {#tbl-ch04-uv-partition-code}

Walk-through:

1. `forward` maps the option to the solver code and throws `UV partition solver requires disjoint vapor-cloud
   reactions` when `partition` is forced on an ineligible network; `auto` on an ineligible network silently uses the
   main kernel.
2. `equilibrate_uv` calls `equilibrate_uv_partition` first for codes `auto` and `partition`; a return of 0 ends the
   call; otherwise `partition` returns 2 with `[Warning] equilibrate_uv partition did not converge`, and `auto`
   continues into the constrained-least-squares iteration.
3. Inside: inventories from the clamped input, validity (finite, non-negative), the first evaluation, the bracket,
   the Newton loop, and on failure the restoration of the input state with `diag` $= -1$.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Disjoint one-to-one pairs only; shared vapours, gaseous products and multi-gas reactions go to the main kernel
  (`auto`) or are refused (`partition`).
- The gain returned is zero, so `effective_cp` of @sec-ch03-adiabat has no latent term from a partition solve;
  that routine uses `ThermoX`, which never takes this path, but a host that reads `ThermoY`'s gain after a
  partition solve gets no latent information.
- The `ftol` option does not apply: the stop is the energy tolerance $64\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\max(|U_0|, 1)$, and
  `max-iter` counts the initial evaluation.
- The bracket search halves or doubles the temperature up to 64 times; a card whose curves are not monotone in
  $F$ may bracket a wrong root. Not measured.
- A pair with $a_j \ne b_j$ is handled by the formulas but untested at the pin.
:::
